channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: WordPress 7.1.5 closes 20 security holes and urges immediate updates
item.description: WordPress released 7.1.5 with fixes for SQL injection, privilege escalation, cross-site scripting, REST and XML-RPC information disclosure, and a Template Part flaw that could lead to remote code execution. Maintainers recommend updating immediately; applicable fixes are also being backported through branch 4.7.

item.title: Entrepreneurs On Fire sells for up to $9 million
item.description: The independent business podcast Entrepreneurs On Fire has been sold to Pathos Communications for $3 million in cash plus as much as $6 million in performance payments. Founder John Lee Dumas will remain host for at least three years, making the deal a revealing valuation of a profitable, personality-led podcast brand.

item.title: Archive Team races to preserve Apple’s support forums before Friday shutdown
item.description: Archive Team lists Apple Discussions as an urgent preservation project before the Apple Support Community closes November 20. The user-to-user troubleshooting archive dates to the 1998 Apple Tech Exchange, making the rescue an unusually large effort to retain practical personal-computing history that Apple has not promised to keep online.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 reaches its first release candidate
item.description: WordPress 7.2 RC1 is available for testing ahead of the December 8 final release. Recent fixes cover media uploads, accessibility, revision previews, plugin dependencies and the Interactivity API; plugin and theme authors are urged to complete compatibility testing without using RC1 on production sites.

item.title: Overcast tests manual ad skipping while trying to protect creators
item.description: Independent podcast app Overcast is testing Smart Skip for premium users. It detects an ad break but never skips automatically, stops before the final call to action and ignores a show’s own membership or product promotions—an attempt by developer Marco Arment to meet listener demand without undermining open-feed economics.

item.title: A 10,000-site crawl finds RSS alive but increasingly hidden
item.description: A crawl of the 10,000 most popular domains found a discoverable working feed on 24% of readable sites. RSS accounted for 94% of working feeds, but 57% of sites that advertised one in 2016 no longer do; several still update the old address, suggesting feed discovery has declined faster than feed publishing.

item.title: AT Protocol prepares a public beta for permissioned data spaces
item.description: AT Protocol will open the public beta of Spaces on December 1. The new layer lets developers build permissioned communities and private or semi-private data sets while keeping accounts portable across applications; updated personal data servers and development tools are available now.

item.title: Apple prepares to bring video podcasts to Apple TV
item.description: Apple is preparing an Apple Podcasts app for Apple TV, giving video podcasters another route to the living room. Podnews says the app will support synchronized playback across devices and arrive as video becomes a larger part of podcast distribution without replacing standard feed delivery.

item.title: Maria Ressa argues journalism must confront platform power
item.description: Nobel laureate Maria Ressa describes how concentrated platform ownership weakened the shared facts democracies need and left journalism struggling to hold power accountable. Her prescription joins newsroom independence, public-interest technology and sustained civic pressure rather than treating the information crisis as a simple product problem.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 introduces a standard Secrets API
item.description: WordPress 7.2 will give core, plugins and hosts a common way to store credentials encrypted at rest. The API supports rotation, versioned values and a host-provided drop-in, while self-hosted installations must define WP_SECRETS_KEY before secrets can be saved.

item.title: The Bulwark and Vox Media form broad current-affairs partnership
item.description: Vox Media will handle advertising, podcast hosting and cross-promotion for The Bulwark under a partnership promising nearly 200 hours of current-affairs programming each month in 2027. The deal joins a growing independent political newsroom with Vox’s distribution and sales infrastructure.

item.title: Atmosphere cooperative organizes builders around the open social web
item.description: Developers, organizers and artists have launched the Atmosphere Community Cooperative to build shared tools, services and community around AT Protocol. Its member-governed structure is an experiment in giving the people who create an interoperable social ecosystem a direct stake in its direction.

item.title: Podnews maps podcast apps by open feature support
item.description: Podnews updated its searchable catalog of newer podcast apps, with filters for transcripts, chapters, funding, location, alternate enclosures, people and value payments. The list makes it easier to see which players implement Podcasting 2.0 features across mobile, desktop and the web.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 adds random discovery across posts and archives
item.description: WordPress 7.2 will add a /random/ route that redirects visitors to a random published post and can also work inside category and author archives. Site owners can customize the base, exclude post types or disable the feature, creating a built-in path back into older writing.

item.title: Raj Shamani’s Figuring Out passes 22 million subscribers
item.description: Podnews reports that Figuring Out with Raj Shamani has reached 22.1 million YouTube subscribers, moving ahead of The Diary of a CEO and The Joe Rogan Experience. The India-based show launched in 2021, a striking shift in the global center of gravity for creator-led podcast video.
